questions.q: To maximize profit while reducing wasted capital, a workshop manager implements a 'Just-In-Time' (JIT) parts inventory strategy. What is the primary operational risk associated with this specific method in a GSM repair business?
options: Accumulating too much obsolete stock of old phone screens.
Exponentially increased physical storage and warehouse costs.
Extended repair turnaround times if external parts suppliers experience shipping delays.
Rapid depreciation of the technician's specialized soldering equipment.
questions.explain: The JIT inventory method involves ordering components strictly as they are requested by customers. While it frees up capital and reduces 'dead stock', any supply chain or courier delay immediately halts the repair, leading to angry customers waiting for their devices.

questions.q: To systematically maximize labor profit margins in a bustling mobile workshop, management relentlessly monitors the 'First-Time Fix Rate' (FTFR). From a purely operational standpoint, what does a high FTFR fundamentally signify?
options: A high statistical percentage of completely new customers are entering the shop weekly.
Technical repairs are being completed accurately on the first attempt, vastly minimizing unpaid warranty reworks and protecting core labor efficiency.
Technicians are physically rushing through repairs much faster than the allotted scheduled invoice time.
The shop management is artificially overcharging clients for basic initial diagnostic tasks.
questions.explain: The 'First-Time Fix Rate' is a critical profit metric. A high FTFR means devices are diagnosed and repaired flawlessly on the first try. Low FTFR means technicians waste expensive labor hours opening up previously fixed phones to correct mistakes for free under warranty.

questions.q: What is a universally effective, supplementary retail strategy rapidly utilized to drastically expand total net profit margins in a GSM repair shop without mathematically raising the primary baseline labor rates?
options: Completely disabling the commercial shop's climate control HVAC system indefinitely to cut minor power usage.
Actively upselling high-margin complementary lifestyle accessories such as impact-resistant cases, tempered glass screen protectors, and braided fast-chargers at the final point of sale.
Covertly utilizing rejected, defective counterfeit hardware components while heavily marketing them as brand new original items.
Refusing to pay junior diagnostic technicians legally mandated minimum wage frameworks.
questions.explain: Secondary accessory attachments (like tempered glass or cases) harbor exceptionally high profit percentage markups and demand practically zero extra technician labor time to install, instantly boosting the average customer ticket size seamlessly alongside the base repair.

questions.q: Your wholesale logistics manager purchases a heavily discounted pallet of lithium replacement batteries loudly branded as 'OEM Original'. Upon deep lab load-testing, the cells experience rapid cyclical depletion and voltage sagging. Operating on core strategic business management logic, what is your most viable long-term reaction?
options: Blindly install the defective cells into daily repairs to artificially force margin retention, since the massive shipment invoice is already cleared.

Instantly halt integration, systematically log the voltage discrepancies, demand an immediate aggressive supplier refund, and dynamically re-source from a rigorously vetted vendor to safeguard shop reputation.
Deceptively parcel and liquidate the defective battery stock onto internet retail sites labeled as 'Perfect Genuine Replacements' to quietly recoup the total loss.
Exclusively reserve the unstable batteries to act strictly as test bench models only for devices requiring rapid glass replacements.
questions.explain: Protecting top-tier business integrity is paramount to survival. Integrating knowingly catastrophic or volatile power cells triggers a massive wave of immediate angry customer warranty returns, totally destroying online store reviews and crippling long-term future profitability.
